$comment: The layering contract. tools/check-boundaries.mjs enforces this in CI. Edit deliberately.

packages/core.why: core must run identically on device, in a browser, and in a test with no platform at all.

packages/data.why: data is a query layer, not a view layer. Hooks belong in ui/.

packages/ui.why: hooks run under BOTH renderers. Importing either one forks this package.

packages/map.purpose: One <Map> interface; the per-platform adapters live behind it.
packages/map.why: the ONLY package allowed to know that maplibre-gl and maplibre-react-native differ. react-native is listed because the NATIVE half of this package renders native views; the web half renders a div. That split is the reason this package exists, so both platform imports belong here and nowhere else.

apps/mobile.why: an app that imports a map SDK directly can define its own layers, and the two apps drift apart visually. Go through @app/map. Font loading is listed here on purpose: expo-font is an asset loader, and the app shell is the only layer that may register assets. @app/ui-native NAMES the faces (type.ts) and must not load them, or it would need a platform asset pipeline and stop being drawable by anything else.

apps/web.why: web hosts BOTH form factors: mobile web renders @app/ui-native via react-native-web, desktop renders its own DOM components. Layer definitions still live in the generated style, never in an app.

packages/ui-native.purpose: Phone components (RN primitives). Shared by the native app AND mobile web.
packages/ui-native.why: must render under react-native AND react-native-web. Touching react-dom breaks the native app; touching a map SDK bypasses @app/map. react-native-svg is allowed HERE and nowhere else: it is a drawing primitive that renders under both, and it is the reason there is no charting library. It is deliberately NOT granted to packages/ui — a hook that could reach for a drawing primitive would start returning elements, and the desktop component set stops being free the moment that happens.

packages/data/src/bundle/drivers.purpose: The only place a platform database may be named.
packages/data/src/bundle/drivers.why: A driver satisfies `Db` — four methods — and nothing above it knows which one it got. That is what lets one query layer serve node:sqlite in tests, a wasm build range-reading R2 on the web, and expo-sqlite on the phone. `packages/data` itself must never name a database: the moment a query reaches for a driver directly, the other two platforms stop being possible.

packages/data/src/spots.purpose: The user's own records, and the only writable store in the app.
packages/data/src/spots.why: A spot is the one thing here that cannot be re-downloaded, and it lives in a store of its own because the regulation bundle is replaced wholesale on every update. This layer may name a FILE system (that is its job) and may never touch the bundle's database — the two must not be able to share a file by accident.

$comment2: testOnlyImports are permitted in *.test.ts / *.test.tsx ONLY. Test files are not shipped, but they are still boundary-checked: a test importing react-native into core is the same architectural smell as source doing it. @testing-library/react is here because it is the only way to MOUNT a ui-native component — it renders through react-native-web, which is the mobile-web target. It pulls react-dom, which ui-native source may never touch; that is precisely why it is test-only and not in mayImport.
